See also: GİK

Cornish

Etymology

From Cornish dialect English geek (“to look, peep, stare intently”).

Noun

gik m (plural gikys)

  1. peep

Derived terms

  • heb gul gik na mik (“stock-still”)
  • na gik na mik (“not a sound”)

Zhuang

Pronunciation

  • (Standard Zhuang) IPA(key): /kik˥/
  • Tone numbers: gig7
  • Hyphenation: gik

Etymology 1

Adjective

gik (Sawndip forms 𰔅 or ⿰其手 or ⿰不居 or 㥍 or 恄 or ⿱吉心 or 极 or 吉, 1957–1982 spelling gik)

  1. lazy
    Synonyms: hwetraez, (dialectal) gyanx, (dialectal) roegrad

Etymology 2

From Chinese 激 (MC kek).

Verb

gik (Sawndip forms 㥛 or 亟, 1957–1982 spelling gik)

  1. to anger; to make mad; to tick off
  2. to mock; to ridicule
    Synonym: (dialectal) gig
  3. to encourage; to motivate

Etymology 3

Noun

gik (1957–1982 spelling gik)

  1. clod of earth made from ploughing
    Synonyms: (dialectal) buenqcae, (dialectal) fwenqcae, (dialectal) gangjga
  2. sod
  3. adobe; mud brick
